counterexample.observed: The crash lands between the durable inventory debit and the separate durable order-completion transaction. Lease recovery applies order-1 twice, producing two movements and 0 units, then rejects the otherwise satisfiable order-2. This violates exact inventory effects, request-id idempotency, and recovery availability.
sequence: Submit order-1 for 7 widgets and durably enqueue it.
A worker leases order-1, inventory durably debits 7 widgets, and the worker is stopped before the separate order-completion transaction commits.
Advance logical time past the 30000-millisecond lease.
A replacement worker leases the same order-1 and inventory accepts it as a second movement, leaving 0 widgets.
Submit order-2 for the remaining 7 widgets; the worker must reject it because the duplicate order-1 effect consumed its capacity.

invariants: Inventory effects are exact: a request ID may apply at most its requested quantity to durable stock, and every accepted effect must fit the stock recorded at that moment.

A request ID is an external idempotency key: once it has produced an inventory movement, any later delivery of that same request ID must reuse that durable result rather than apply another inventory effect.
An expired worker lease is retried without losing the order; recovery must preserve both availability and the prior durable inventory effect.
name: durable-reservation-retry
plausible_wrong_fix: Add a process-local set of request IDs in the worker to skip repeat deliveries; the set vanishes in the crash that causes redelivery, so the replacement worker still debits stock again.
